# Hard stops (HS-v1)

These apply to every session, every role, every card. If a step would cross
one, stop the step, write what was needed in your return file with status
`BLOCKED`, and do nothing else for that step.

- **HS-1 Live data.** Never open, list, read, copy, back up, restore or

  coordinator gave you. Never merge into `main`, pull, rebase, reset,
  force-push, rewrite history, or change repository visibility. Stage

- **HS-5 Secrets.** Never create, print, copy or commit a production
  signing key or password. Test keys live only inside a sandbox run folder.

- **HS-7 Safety instruments.** Never loosen a scorer, guard, lock, test or

## Fixed decisions
C-ACQ@1 rules 1 to 7, in full, and these say how each one is reached.

1. **Where the approved redirect hosts come from, and in what order.** A07's
   redirect cell is a placeholder, and the catalogue has no redirect concept at
   all (one global `ALLOWED_DOWNLOAD_HOSTS`, `catalog.ts:36`, consumed by
   `assertAllowedHost`, which knows nothing of redirects). So the probe is
   **step 1**: `node scripts/v2/probe-redirects.mjs` runs before any test needs
   an approved redirect host, writes
   `docs/v2/evidence/P4.1/redirects.md`, and the hosts it recorded are the only
   candidates. Step 2 admits them under this rule and no other: a host goes into
   an allowance's `allowedRedirectHosts` **iff** (a) the probe recorded it as a
   `Location` host for that artifact, and (b) it ends in `huggingface.co` or
   `hf.co` on a dot boundary, case-insensitively — the mechanical form of A07's
   "only Hugging Face CDN hosts". A host failing (b), or one the probe saw but
   cannot attribute to a single artifact, is stop condition 1, never an
   admission. A probe that records no `Location` at all leaves the list empty,
   and an empty list is the correct answer, not a gap. The two allowances are
   named in `catalog.ts` — `SPEECH_DOWNLOAD_ALLOWANCE` for the two speech
   entries, `C_STT_CANDIDATE_ALLOWANCE` for the six C-STT candidates — each
   `{ allowedHosts: readonly string[]; allowedRedirectHosts: readonly string[] }`,
   and `downloadWithResume` takes the one matching the artifact it is fetching,
   so rule 2 is per artifact and not a second global list. `catalog.ts` stays the
   only file in the package naming a host (`catalog.test.ts:77-92` keeps
   asserting that), and `ALLOWED_DOWNLOAD_HOSTS` is the union of every allowance's
   `allowedHosts` **and** `allowedRedirectHosts`, plus the hosts the licence
   pages already name (`registry.ollama.ai`); a test asserts that union. The
   admitted redirect hosts enter through the allowances' `allowedRedirectHosts`,
   so they are included by construction — there is no second, separate list.
2. **The code vocabulary, and where it lives.** One closed union declared in the
   new `installer/src/readiness.ts` and exported from there, so the request
   guard and the readiness verdict speak the same words. Readiness is
   `state: 'missing' | 'ready' | 'invalid'`, and `invalid` carries exactly one
   code: `size_mismatch` (the size is not the pinned `sizeBytes` — what the
   11-byte and zero-byte cases assert), `hash_mismatch` (a fresh hash did not
   match the pinned digest), `not_a_regular_file` (a directory, or a symlink
   resolving to one — `lstatSync`, not `statSync`), `stale_pin` (the `.part`
   sidecar's `url` or `checksum` is not the pin the catalogue holds now,
   `resume.ts:58-63`), `dangling_part` (a `.part` with no sidecar, or with one
   that does not describe it), `no_pinned_hash` (the entry pins neither `sha256`
   nor `sha1`; the existing refusal at `run.ts:256-262`, kept). Request
   refusals, same file: `scheme_not_https`, `port_not_allowed`,
   `user_info_present`, `fragment_present`, `query_not_allowed`,
   `query_key_not_allowed`, `host_not_allowed`, `too_many_hops`,
   `redirect_loop`. `query_not_allowed` is a row that admits no query at all;
   `query_key_not_allowed` is a query carrying a parameter name outside the
   row's *Allowed query keys* cell. `ACQUISITION.md` §1 now carries that cell
   and its rule (AM-042, owner-approved): A07 enumerates the ten names its
   artifacts actually present, and every other row is `none`, which is the
   pre-existing behaviour. The catalogue gains a per-entry
   `allowedQueryKeys`, empty for every entry but the six C-STT ones; the check
   is membership of the **name** set, never a prefix, wildcard or blanket
   permission, and it runs before the URL is requested. No value is ever read,
   logged, recorded or compared. No code enters
   `SETUP_ERROR_CODES` and none reaches the JSONL in this card: a refusal thrown
   by the downloader surfaces through today's `describeFailure` as `unexpected`
   carrying the refusal sentence as its `override` (`errors.ts:118-124`), and
   P4.4 is what puts a code on the wire. When P4.4 does give one a sentence, the
   banned-words regex at `errors.test.ts:20-27` still forbids "checksum",
   `SHA-?n` and `HTTP n` in the prose, so `hash_mismatch` and `size_mismatch`
   are identifiers only.
3. **The verdict reaches `ProbedState` as a boolean, not as a widened field.**
   `readiness.ts` returns the verdict and its code; `probeState` derives the
   three booleans from `state === 'ready'` and from nothing else.
   `ProbedState` keeps three `boolean`s and gains no member, so `plan.ts` and
   `protocol.ts` stay out of scope and `buildPlan` keeps receiving booleans at
   `run.ts:132-139`. Putting the code on the wire is P4.4's, and only P4.4's.
4. **The receipt, pinned verbatim.** `<modelsDir>/<file>.receipt.json`, mode
   `0o600`, one JSON object, no other keys and no trailing fields:

   ```json
   {
     "version": 1,
     "filename": "ggml-tiny.en.bin",
     "algorithm": "sha256",
     "digest": "921e4cf8686fdd993dcd081a5da5b6c365bfde1162e72b08d75ac75289920b1f",
     "sizeBytes": 77704715,
     "mtimeMs": 1758230400000,
     "dev": 66310,
     "ino": 4242
   }
   ```

   - `version` is `1`; any other value, or a file that will not parse, counts as
     no receipt.
   - `algorithm` is `"sha256"` when the entry pins one and `"sha1"` when it does
     not. That is the `sha256: null` case: the receipt records the SHA-1 the
     catalogue does pin (`run.ts:212`) and the download path is unchanged. Both
     null is `no_pinned_hash` — refused, never downloaded.
   - `mtimeMs` is `Math.floor(stat.mtimeMs)`: integer milliseconds, because
     `fs.Stats` reports ms everywhere and an `mtimeNs` field would need a
     `bigint` stat and a second comparison rule. A file whose mtime moved at all
     — a restore, a copy that did not preserve it — fails the match and is
     hashed once more. Correctness is worth one hash of 75 MiB.
   - `dev` and `ino` are the inode identity `statSync` reports, as two JSON
     numbers; both are safe integers on Linux and macOS for a file this size.
     Together they are "inode" for rule 5, and a file copied onto another volume
     fails them even with the same size, mtime and digest.
   - **Written only** after a fresh hash matched, or after `commitDownload`
     renamed the verified `.part` into place — never while a `.part` exists, and
     never before verification.
   - **Rewritten in full** after any repair, and the old receipt goes with the
     file it described. A receipt whose `filename`, `algorithm`, `digest` or
     `sizeBytes` disagrees with the catalogue is treated as no receipt: hash
     once, rewrite it.
   - A missing receipt is not a failure, it is the hash-it-once path a fresh
     install and a restored backup both take.
   - P4.3, P4.4 and S4b.1 read this shape. Nothing else may.
5. **The pinned size is a pin.** `SpeechModelEntry` gains
   `readonly sizeBytes: number` beside `approxBytes`, and `SPEECH_MODEL` and
   `PREVIEW_SPEECH_MODEL` pin `77_704_715` — the measured count that survives
   today only in the `approxBytes` comment (`catalog.ts:93-99`). `approxBytes`
   stays and keeps its one job, refusing a download on a full disk before it
   starts; `sizeBytes` is what rule 5's "size equals the pinned size" means, and
   it is what the 11-byte, zero-byte and wrong-build cases are asserted against.
   A verified file whose size is not `sizeBytes` is `size_mismatch`; a **second**
   mismatch on the same artifact after a repair is stop condition 5, because
   re-downloading cannot fix a wrong pin.
6. **The test transport is an injected `fetch`, and nothing else.** There is no
   HTTPS test server in this card. `DownloadOptions.fetchImpl` and
   `SetupEnvironment.fetchImpl` are both `typeof fetch` (`download.ts:42`,
   `run.ts:38`), so there is nowhere to pass a dispatcher that would trust a
   self-signed certificate, and the only host a loopback server can offer is one
   `assertAllowedHost` must refuse — the hole `download.test.ts:12-19` declines
   to open on purpose. Tests inject a `fetch` that answers from memory, keep the
   **real pinned URL** so rule 1 runs for real, and open no socket. No test
   binds a port, no test certificate exists, `127.0.0.1` never enters any
   allow-list, and the "exemption cannot spread" scan at `catalog.test.ts:77-92`
   keeps passing.
7. **A hop is one redirect followed.** The initial request is hop 0 and is not
   counted. Each `Location` is resolved against the current URL, validated under
   rule 1, checked against that artifact's `allowedRedirectHosts`, and only then
   requested — that request is hop 1, and at most 5 hops may be followed. A 6th
   `Location` fails with `too_many_hops` before it is requested. A `Location`
   that resolves to a URL already requested for this download (the initial URL
   or any earlier hop, compared as the absolute string
   `new URL(location, current).href` produces) fails with `redirect_loop` before
   it is requested. And the only header the downloader ever sends is `Range`, on
   the initial request alone: a redirect hop carries no header at all, so a
   resumed download that meets a redirect restarts from byte 0 at the new host
   rather than asking it for a range it was never offered the whole of. No
   custom header exists anywhere in `download.ts` and none is added.
8. **The probe's URLs come from the built catalogue, and it holds no host
   literal.** `scripts/v2/probe-redirects.mjs` imports `SPEECH_MODEL` and
   `PREVIEW_SPEECH_MODEL` from `installer/dist/catalog.js` (built by
   `npm run build --workspace @apunta/installer`; `dist/` is gitignored and
   rebuilt per row). `eslint.config.js` exempts exactly one file,
   `installer/src/catalog.ts` (`:144`), the probe is not that file, and a literal
   in it fails V3 — so the script names no host. It requests
   `SPEECH_MODEL.url` and `PREVIEW_SPEECH_MODEL.url` (the same file;
   `catalog.test.ts:111-120` pins the two entries equal, so this is one request
   recorded under both entry names) and the six C-STT candidates — `ggml-base.bin`,
   `ggml-base-q5_1.bin`, `ggml-small.bin`, `ggml-small-q5_1.bin`,
   `ggml-large-v3-turbo-q5_0.bin`, `ggml-large-v3-turbo-q8_0.bin`
   (`CONTRACTS.md:450-452`) — by substituting each filename into
   `SPEECH_MODEL.url`'s path. Seven requests, six distinct artifacts. Building a
   URL from fragments so the lint selector misses is forbidden: that is
   loosening a guard (HS-7). If the built catalogue cannot be imported, V2 is
   `BLOCKED`; it is never a reason to add an exemption.
9. **Rule 7 lives in the installer's own Ollama client.** `installer/src/ollama.ts`
   gains a digest read: after a successful `pullModel`, one `POST /api/show` for
   that tag over the same loopback `fetchImpl`, and the tag with its digest is
   reported in the existing `message` event's text — no wire change, because
   `message` already carries free text. The daemon's own network behaviour stays
   outside these checks and the message says so in as many words, because that
   is what rule 7's last clause requires; the same statement goes in
   `WritingModelEntry`'s doc comment in `catalog.ts`, which is why no doc outside
   May edit is needed for it. No pull is started for a tag `hasModel` already
   reports (`ollama.ts:76-94`; A08 and HS-3), and no tag is ever removed or
   replaced: the client has no such call and this card adds none. HS-3's Ollama
   clauses are therefore met by construction, not by a stop condition.
10. **Repair happens only after the user presses Start.** Readiness is computed
    on every run and repairs nothing. The repair — `discardDownload`, then
    `downloadWithResume` — happens only inside the step the user's Start press
    began (`run.ts:175-193`). A run that only probes, such as the one behind the
    plan, writes nothing on disk.

## Egress (this card only)
HS-3 permits only what `docs/v2/ACQUISITION.md` lists, and it lists no row for
probing a download host, so this card states its own grant and its own limits,
in P1.5's shape (`docs/v2/cards/P1.5.md:108-118`).

- **The exact URL set:** the seven in Fixed decision 8 — the two speech entries'
  one URL, and the six C-STT candidate paths — and nothing else. No other host,
  no other path, no sub-resource, no retry against a different host, no
  `Range`.
- **Method:** `HEAD` only, with `redirect: 'manual'`. The `Location` is read
  from the response and never followed. A `GET` is not authorised by this card
  and no response body is ever read.
- **No credentials**, no query of its own, no fragment, no cookie jar, no custom
  header. Whatever `User-Agent` Node sends is left alone.
- **No bytes are acquired.** Nothing is downloaded or installed, no model is
  pulled, and no Ollama daemon is contacted by the probe at all. Rule 7's
  `/api/show` in Fixed decision 9 is a loopback call the installer's own runtime
  client makes, reached only through `SetupEnvironment.ollamaBaseUrl`, and is
  exercised only by a test with an injected `fetch`.
- **Logged:** the method, the request URL, the response status, each `Location`
  host in hop order with its scheme, port and query-presence verdict, the hop
  count and the date, into `docs/v2/evidence/P4.1/redirects.md`, which the script
  writes itself. Per artifact, `ACQUISITION.md` §1's item fields are recorded as
  "not acquired — HEAD only, no bytes": there is no size and no SHA-256 in that
  file because none was computed, and a reviewer is not left hunting for one.
- **Sanitisation by construction:** the script writes no machine, user or
  container identifier — no `os.hostname()`, no login name, no home or sandbox
  path — so RUN-CONFIG §4's bar is met without redacting the one thing the file
  exists to record. The only paths it writes are the repository-relative
  evidence path and the catalogue's own public URLs. An observed query string is
  written `<redacted>`, never pasted; an observed host is the artefact's content
  and is written as observed, the way `docs/v2/evidence/P1.5/licence-evidence.md`
  records a public vendor URL. Stop condition 4 covers the case where the
  coordinator reads §4 more widely than this.
- `CLAUDE.md` hard rule 1's model-acquisition carve-out covers the installer
  process, not an agent's ad-hoc fetch, and is **not** relied on here: this
  grant is the card's own, it covers the step 1 probe and the V2 re-run and
  nothing else, and it is spent when V2 completes.

## Steps
1. **Probe first** (Fixed decision 8, under the Egress grant above). Run
   `node scripts/v2/probe-redirects.mjs`; it writes
   `docs/v2/evidence/P4.1/redirects.md`. This is first because it is the only
   source of the approved redirect hosts, and the "approved redirect" case in
   step 3 cannot be written before it exists.
2. **Admit the observed hosts** (Fixed decision 1): put exactly the hosts that
   passed both tests into the two allowances in `catalog.ts`, extend
   `ALLOWED_DOWNLOAD_HOSTS` by exactly those hosts, and update
   `catalog.test.ts:26` to the new list. The scan at `catalog.test.ts:77-92`
   stays true. A host that fails either test is stop condition 1, not an edit.
3. **Tests first,** each case with the observable it asserts — a scenario with
   no observable is not a case:

   | # | Case | What it asserts |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | 1 | approved direct download | exactly one fetch call, to the pinned URL; 200; the file committed at its final name; a receipt written |
   | 2 | approved redirect | two fetch calls, the pinned URL then the admitted CDN URL; final 200; the committed bytes byte-identical to the fixture; the second call's `init.headers` is empty |
   | 3 | redirect to an unlisted host | exactly one fetch call recorded and the unlisted URL appears in none; refusal code `host_not_allowed`; no second request was made |
   | 4 | `http:` redirect | one call; `scheme_not_https`, and the exact `Location` in the message |
   | 5 | user-info URL | zero calls; `user_info_present`; refused before contact |
   | 6 | port 8443 | zero calls; `port_not_allowed`; refused before contact |
   | 7 | fragment in the URL | zero calls; `fragment_present` |
   | 8 | query in the URL on a row that admits none | zero calls; `query_not_allowed` |
   | 8a | query whose names are all in the row's *Allowed query keys* | the URL is requested; the admitted query survives redirect admission unchanged, and the download completes and verifies against the pinned `sha256` |
   | 8b | query carrying one name outside that cell | zero calls; `query_key_not_allowed`; refused before contact, and the exact name is in the message |
   | 9 | redirect loop | two calls, then `redirect_loop`; the repeated URL is never requested a second time |
   | 10 | 5 hops | six calls, the file committed — the success boundary beside case 11 |
   | 11 | 6 hops | six calls, then `too_many_hops`, and the 6th `Location` was never requested |
   | 12 | no custom headers to any host | for every hop the recorded `init.headers` is empty, and on a resumed download the `Range` goes to the first host only while the redirect hop re-requests the whole file |
   | 13 | checksum mismatch | `discardDownload` ran; no committed file, no receipt; the existing `checksum_mismatch` failure |
   | 14 | interrupted `.part` resume | the second run sends `Range: bytes=<n>-`, gets 206, appends, verifies, commits and writes the receipt |
   | 15 | 11-byte file at the model path | `invalid` with `size_mismatch` against the pinned `sizeBytes`; not `ready`; nothing written, nothing repaired |
   | 16 | zero-byte file | `invalid` with `size_mismatch`, not `missing` |
   | 17 | directory at the path | `invalid` with `not_a_regular_file`, and the same through a symlink to a directory |
   | 18 | stale receipt after the file changed | the receipt's `mtimeMs` no longer matches, so the file is hashed once more and the receipt is rewritten; a receipt whose `digest` disagrees with the pin is treated as no receipt and takes the same path |
   | 19 | valid receipt | zero fetch calls and zero hash calls — neither the downloader nor `hashFile` is reached — and `ready` |
   | 20 | an entry with `sha256: null` | the receipt is written with `algorithm: "sha1"` and the SHA-1 digest; an entry with neither pinned is `no_pinned_hash` and issues no request |
   | 21 | dangling `.part` | `invalid` with `dangling_part`; the bytes are removed before a repair |
   | 22 | sidecar pinning an older file | `invalid` with `stale_pin`; a fresh download, no append |
   | 23 | rule 7's digest | after a successful pull, one `POST /api/show` for that tag and the message names tag and digest; a tag `hasModel` already reports issues no `/api/pull` at all, and no call removes or replaces a tag |

   Record the failures. Every case must fail on the base commit or be recorded
   as the behaviour that already exists.
4. **Implement** (Fixed decisions 2 to 10) in that order: the union and the
   guard, then the pinned size, then the receipt, then the redirect loop, then
   the digest read. V2 then re-runs the probe against the finished catalogue and
   its run is the record of record: `redirects.md` is overwritten with that

   moved, or because a CDN changed its mind between the two — record both, say
   which one the admitted hosts came from, and let the disagreement be a stop
   condition 1 decision rather than a silent overwrite.

# Contract excerpts (authoritative)

## C-ACQ@1 Acquisition and readiness

**Built by** P4.1. **Proven by** P4.1, P4.4, S4b.1. **Consumers:** installer,
setup screens, Spanish speech acquisition.

**Requests**
1. `https:` only; port absent or 443; no user-info; no fragment; no query
   unless the artifact's manifest entry lists allowed query keys.
2. Host must be in the artifact's `allowedHosts` (initial) or
   `allowedRedirectHosts` (redirects) in `ACQUISITION.md`.
3. `redirect: 'manual'`. Each `Location` is resolved and validated **before**
   it is requested. At most 5 hops; a repeated URL is a loop and fails.
   No custom headers are sent to any host.
4. Checksum verification stays separate and mandatory.

**Readiness**
5. A model file is ready only if it is a regular file (not a directory or
   symlink to one), its size equals the pinned size, and either a receipt
   `<file>.receipt.json` records the pinned SHA-256 with matching size,
   mtime and inode, or a fresh hash matches (then a receipt is written).
6. Wrong size, wrong hash, directory, stale pin or dangling `.part` →
   state `invalid` with a code; repair only after the user presses Start.
7. Ollama pulls are performed by the daemon, outside these checks. The
   installer verifies the resulting tag's digest with `ollama show` and
   reports it; it cannot enforce the daemon's network behaviour, and the
   docs say so.

**Protocol.** The existing JSON-lines protocol (`installer/src/protocol.ts`)
stays the only one. Additions are optional fields. Exactly one terminal
event per run (`done` or `failed`). Cancel sends SIGTERM to the installer's
own process group only.

**Rejection examples.** Initial URL `https://huggingface.co:8443/…` → refused
before contact. Redirect to a host not listed → refused before contact.
11-byte file at the model path → `invalid`, not ready.

**Redirect admission (rule 1).** A redirect is followed only when its `Location`
resolves to `https:`, port 443, no user-info, no fragment, a host the row's
*Redirect hosts* cell admits, and a query whose every parameter name appears in
that row's *Allowed query keys* cell. A parameter name outside the cell is
refused (`query_key_not_allowed`) before the URL is requested. `none` means the
row admits no query at all, so any query is `query_not_allowed` — that is the
default and it is unchanged. No row admits a query by wildcard, a prefix or a
blanket permission, and the cell is the complete list: adding a name is a
plan-editor amendment (AM-042).

**Why A07's names are safe to enumerate.** The ten names are the AWS
CloudFront signed-URL parameter set plus Hugging Face's Xet and
`response-content-*` parameters, observed on 2026-09-26 across all six C-STT
artifacts and the one speech artifact, each answering `302` to
`us.aws.cdn.hf.co` (`docs/v2/evidence/P4.1/redirects.md`). They cannot change
*which* bytes arrive: the path is fixed by the pinned catalogue URL and the
bytes are verified against the pinned `sha256`, and the committed name is the
entry's own `sizeBytes` path, so the two `response-content-*` parameters can
only shape headers a client would have sent anyway. The card's own worry — "a
query string is where a download URL turns into a message" — is about
*outbound* data, and none of these names carries any: the probe records the
**names** only and writes every value as `<redacted>`, so a signature is never
in the repository, the evidence or any log.

**Owner-run items.** `apt` needs `sudo`. The coordinator writes the exact
command to `docs/v2/state/OWNER-ACTIONS.md`, stops the dependent cards, and
waits; the owner runs it. Agents never enter a password.

**Ollama.** Before any pull, run `ollama list`; if the tag exists, do not pull.
Record the digest with `ollama show <tag>`. Real-model runs set Ollama's
`keep_alive` so evaluation models unload after use, and run only one model
at a time, to avoid starving the live instance.

## 2. Development tools already present

Anything already installed on the PC (git, Python, Piper if present,
whisper-cli, Ollama) may be used as found. Record its version in evidence.

## 3. L-POLICY@1 Licences

One rule, applied per object reviewed (a tool, a library, a model file, a
voice, a dictionary, generated audio are separate objects).

| Object | Allowed |
| --- | --- |
| Code or data **shipped** in the app or installer | MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, ISC, Zlib, 0BSD, Unicode, OFL-1.1 (fonts), CC0, CC-BY-4.0 (data, with attribution) |
| The one pre-approved exception | Spanish dictionary **data** under an MPL option of a multi-licence, shipped unmodified in its own files, election and obligations stated in `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` and `docs/decisions.md` |
| Development-only tools never shipped or linked | any OSI licence, including GPL (Piper) |
| Generated fixtures committed to the repo | only if the voice's model card permits redistribution of generated audio; otherwise generate at test time into the sandbox and never commit |
| Models downloaded by the user at setup | per the publisher's licence, shown in setup, recorded in the catalogue |
| System libraries bundled into an AppImage (for example WebKitGTK, LGPL) | allowed for **test builds**; **public distribution requires owner review** (listed in the final report) |

Anything else: do not add it; the card reports `BLOCKED` with the licence
text found. A dependency's MIT wrapper does not change its data's licence.

## The finding, in one paragraph

All seven pinned artifacts — the speech model and the six C-STT candidates —
answer `302` and send the client to **`us.aws.cdn.hf.co`**. That host ends in
`hf.co` on a dot boundary, so it is inside the Hugging Face domain tree and
**stop condition 1 does not fire**: it is an admissible host on the domain test
alone. But **every one of the seven `Location`s carries a query string**, and
each one therefore trips rule 1's `query_not_allowed`. That is stop condition 2,
on every artifact rather than on one edge case, and its remedy is explicitly the
coordinator's: an allowed-query-keys column in `ACQUISITION.md`, or the artifact
marked unavailable. The two probe runs agree exactly, so there is no
"which run did the hosts come from" question to settle.

   requests for seven distinct artifacts.** Fixed decision 8 counts the two

   1 + 6 = 7 requests; the artifact count that follows is 7, not 6, and V2's own
   row says "The six C-STT artifacts **and the one speech artifact** are all
   present". The probe follows V2's reading: seven requests, seven artifacts,
   the speech one recorded under both entry names. Recorded rather than
   silently resolved, because the card's two sentences disagree.

No other deviation. The card's Fixed decisions were not implemented, so none of
them was departed from.

## Unresolved items

1. **The plan-editor action — this is what the card is waiting on.** Stop
   condition 2 names two remedies, and the choice is not this session's:

   - **(a) An allowed-query-keys column in `docs/v2/ACQUISITION.md` §1**, for
     A07's redirect hosts. C-ACQ@1 rule 1 already anticipates it: "no query
     unless the artifact's manifest entry lists allowed query keys" — the
     manifest simply has no such column yet. Whoever fills it will need the key
     names, and **one `HEAD` against the pinned URL reads them**; this card's
     grant did not cover that request and correctly did not make it. The
     narrowest shape that would work: the exception applies to a redirect
     `Location` on an admitted redirect host, and the *initial* request keeps its
     no-query rule, because a query there would be Apunta's own rather than the
     host's.
   - **(b) Mark the artifact unavailable**, which S4a.2's own stop condition
     already permits. Worth naming plainly: on the evidence of this probe that
     leaves the product with no speech model at all, because the pinned file is
     the one Apunta's note and preview both run on.

   Offered as an observation, not a decision (HS-7: rule 1 is the coordinator's
   to change): the risk the card names — "a query string is where a download URL
   turns into a message" — is real but is not the same risk on the two sides of
   a redirect. A query on a request Apunta composes is Apunta leaking something
   of its own. A query the pinned host itself put in a `Location` it handed us is
   that host's own mechanism, scoped to that host and short-lived. That is an
   argument for scoping (a) as narrowly as possible, not for skipping it.

2. **Why the rest of the card was not implemented anyway**, since a reviewer
   will ask. Three reasons, in order of weight:
   - **Implementing rule 1 as written would break a download that works today.**
     `download.ts:98-102` currently issues `redirect: 'follow'`, so first-run
     setup follows this exact 302 to the CDN and the file arrives. Rule 3
     replaces that with `redirect: 'manual'` plus a guard that refuses any
     query — so shipping the guard without the manifest change turns a working
     speech-model download into one that fails at the first hop, on a real
     machine, in a way no test in this card would catch.
   - **Step 3's case 2 cannot be written honestly.** "Approved redirect: the
     pinned URL then the admitted CDN URL" can only be expressed with a
     query-less `Location`, because that is the only shape the guard permits, and
     the real vendor never answers that way. Such a test would pass while the
     product could not make the request.
   - **V1 cannot pass without all 23 cases**, so a partial implementation would
     have no green row to show for it, in a card with one verification table.

   The unblocked work is unchanged by any of this and is ready to pick straight
   up: `readiness.ts` and its verdict codes, the `.receipt.json` shape, the
   `sizeBytes` pin, the `ProbedState` boolean derivation, the per-artifact
   allowance union, and rule 7's `POST /api/show` digest read. None of the ten
   Fixed decisions needs re-deriving; only the query ruling is missing.

3. **A stale comment the coordinator will want to know about, in a file this

4. **Stop condition 4's ruling, asked for the second time.** Does RUN-CONFIG §4's

## Notes for the reviewer

- **What exists:** the probe, and the evidence file it wrote. The probe reads
  every URL out of the built catalogue, holds no URL literal at all, sends
  `HEAD` with `redirect: 'manual'`, never follows a `Location`, never reads a
  body, sends no credential and no custom header, retries nothing, and writes no
  machine, user or container identifier — which is how RUN-CONFIG §4's bar is
  met without redacting the one thing the file exists to record. The six C-STT
  URLs are built by substituting a filename into the pinned speech URL's path,
  never written out as addresses.
- **What does not exist:** `installer/src/readiness.ts`,
  `installer/src/readiness.test.ts`, the two allowance objects, the
  `sizeBytes` pin, the receipt, the redirect loop, the request guard, the
  `ProbedState` derivation, rule 7's digest read, and all 23 test cases.
  `ALLOWED_DOWNLOAD_HOSTS` still holds exactly its three names and
  `assertAllowedHost` is unchanged, so **the shipped guard is exactly as it was
  and the working download path is untouched.**
- **No hard stop (HS-1 … HS-10) was crossed.** The live data folder was never
  opened, listed or copied; port 7717 was never contacted; no server was

  Ollama daemon contacted; the sandbox's `port 7826` is unused and no listener
